rounds.response:
The plaintiff requests that most squarely target our internal emails/forecasting/operations are: (1) any demand for “all internal communications” regarding demand forecasts, production/order changes, or schedule adjustments; (2) requests for communications about specification changes or internal approvals of specs/tolerances; (3) requests for internal operations troubleshooting, root-cause analyses, and staffing/production discussions; and (4) broad custodian/time-period requests seeking “all communications” from operations, supply-chain, or executive custodians.  

Objection/response 1 — Overbreadth/Proportionality: Objection—responsive to the extent the request seeks objectively verifiable, external-facing materials relating to supplier performance (e.g., contracts, POs, shipping records, inspection reports, and supplier emails); otherwise overbroad and disproportionate because it calls for internal, iterative communications across numerous custodians and time periods that are not necessary to prove supplier breaches; we are willing to meet and confer to narrow custodians, date ranges, and search terms before any rolling production. (Use for requests of type 1 and 4.)  

Objection/response 2 — Privilege/Deliberative Process: Objection—calls for internal deliberations, forecasting analyses, and candid operational assessments that are protected by attorney–client privilege and/or work-product and, to the extent applicable, deliberative-process protections; we will withhold privileged materials and will provide a privilege log describing withheld documents. (Use for requests of type 1–3.)  

Objection/response 3 — Relevance/Reasonable Production Commitment: Without waiving objections, Acme will produce non‑privileged, objective documents that directly evidence supplier performance and remedies—signed supply agreement(s), purchase orders, shipment logs (e.g., Shipping_Log_Excerpt_Jan-Apr.xlsx), inspection/failure reports, and direct supplier correspondence regarding delays or defects—while proposing targeted search parameters (limited custodians, specific date ranges around the alleged breaches, and narrowly tailored keywords) to avoid unnecessary disclosure of internal operational chatter. (Use for requests of type 1–4.)
